# Attestto Specifications

> Identity standards and open specifications by the Attestto Identity Standards Group. Hosted at [spec.attestto.com](https://spec.attestto.com). Developed by [Attestto Open](https://attestto.org).

## Specifications hosted here

| Specification | Path | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `did:sns` — DID Method for Solana Name Service | [/did-sns/](https://spec.attestto.com/did-sns/) | Provisional |
| IEAL — Identity Evidence Assurance Level | [/ieal/](https://spec.attestto.com/ieal/) | Working Draft v0.1 |
| IEAL to NIST SP 800-63-4 Crosswalk | [/ieal/crosswalks/nist-800-63/](https://spec.attestto.com/ieal/crosswalks/nist-800-63/) | Informative, not endorsed by NIST |
| VCP — Verifiable Content Provenance | [/vcp/](https://spec.attestto.com/vcp/) | Working Draft v0.1 |

## VCP in one paragraph

VCP is an embed-first content-envelope specification: a signed metadata block carried inside PDF, JPEG, or a sidecar file that binds an issuer DID, a canonical content hash, a timestamp, and an optional IEAL claim to any host file. Legacy readers ignore the block; VCP-aware tools verify it. Reference implementation in `@attestto/vcp` at [github.com/Attestto-com/vcp-cli](https://github.com/Attestto-com/vcp-cli). VCP is intentionally narrow: it answers "who issued this, when, to whom, and has it been modified" and defers rights expression, licensing, and access control to profiles or complementary specifications.

## IEAL in one paragraph

IEAL classifies identity evidence artifacts across three independent axes — Capture (device attestation), Algorithm (presentation-attack detection strength), and Storage (key material protection) — and composes them into a single level L0 through L6. IEAL is designed to fit inside the NIST SP 800-63-4 Subscriber-Controlled Wallet model (§2.4). It is carrier-agnostic: IEAL claims may be carried in W3C Verifiable Credentials, COSE-signed objects, PDF signature dictionaries, C2PA manifests, or a standalone envelope. Reference the axis-by-axis NIST 800-63-4 crosswalk for the formal mapping.

# did:sns — DID Method Specification

> Alias-anchored W3C Decentralized Identifiers for cross-border interoperability, privacy, and compliance. Binds W3C DIDs to human-readable `.sol` Solana Name Service domains.

## What did:sns is

`did:sns` is a W3C DID method that uses Solana Name Service (SNS) `.sol` domains as the primary identifier. It introduces a **Dual-DID architecture** — the `did:sns` identity serves as a permanent, privacy-preserving credential anchor while `alsoKnownAs` links extend reach to Ethereum (ENS), web domains, and legacy systems, without duplicating credentials.

```
did:sns:alice.crbank.sol         ← client subdomain (tenant-issued)
did:sns:crbank.sol               ← institutional root DID
did:sns:alice.attestto.sol       ← platform-issued subdomain
did:sns:attestto.sol             ← platform root DID
did:sns:devnet:alice.attestto.sol ← explicit network qualifier
```

## The problem it solves

Traditional banks, fintechs, and Web3 platforms each maintain identity silos. A customer verified by Bank A re-verifies from scratch at Bank B. Compliance data can't cross chains or institutions. Ethereum identities (ENS) are transparent (full on-chain history) and expire on non-renewal.

`did:sns` solves this with:
- A permanent Solana-anchored identity that doesn't expire
- Bidirectional `alsoKnownAs` links bridging Web2, Ethereum, and Solana ecosystems
- ISO 20022 party data in the DID Document for SWIFT / SINPE / Fedwire compatibility
- GLEIF vLEI bridge for instant institutional KYB
- Zero PII on-chain

## Dual-DID architecture

```
did:sns:alice.crbank.sol
  ├── alsoKnownAs: did:ens:alice.eth        ← Ethereum ecosystem
  ├── alsoKnownAs: did:pkh:solana:CKg5...   ← Universal key-proof layer
  ├── alsoKnownAs: did:web:crbank.cr         ← Bank's web domain
  ├── service: ISO 20022 party data          ← SWIFT/Fedwire/SINPE
  └── service: GLEIF vLEI bridge             ← Instant institutional KYB
```

Both DID Documents must reference each other (`alsoKnownAs` is bidirectional). A unilateral claim is rejected — this prevents identity hijacking if a linked name (e.g. ENS) expires and is re-registered.

## Privacy architecture — 7 layers

The DID Document contains **zero personal data**. Every layer is engineered to minimize what a verifier, on-chain observer, or the platform itself can learn.

1. **No PII on-chain** — Solana stores only cryptographic commitments (hashes, public keys, attestation pointers). Personal data lives in encrypted Vaults with 2-of-N Shamir key splits.
2. **SD-JWT selective disclosure** — per-field salted hashes. A holder proves "I am over 18" without revealing their date of birth.
3. **Pairwise identifiers** — each verifier relationship gets a unique subdomain DID derived from `SHA-256(verifierDID + holderSecret)`. Two verifiers cannot correlate the same holder.
4. **Consent-gated proof access** — no credential is shared without explicit per-field consent. Consent is time-bounded and revocable.
5. **Dual-key Shamir vault** — VMK split across user devices, platform, and guardians. Platform alone cannot decrypt.
6. **Crypto-shredding** — deleting the platform's key share renders vault data permanently inaccessible. Satisfies GDPR Article 17 and Costa Rica Law 8968.
7. **Post-quantum forward secrecy** — hybrid migration path: ML-DSA-44 (FIPS 204) + Ed25519, ML-KEM-768 + X25519.

## DID syntax

```
did:sns:<network-qualifier>:<sns-name>

did:sns:alice.crbank.sol                 ← mainnet (implicit)
did:sns:devnet:alice.crbank.sol          ← devnet
did:sns:testnet:alice.crbank.sol         ← testnet
```

SNS name must be a valid `.sol` domain. Subdomains (`alice.crbank.sol`) map to tenant-issued identities. Root domains (`crbank.sol`) map to institutional identities.

## CRUD operations

- **Create** — Register a `.sol` SNS domain, publish DID Document to Attestto CDN (`attestto.id`), anchor hash to Solana via SAS
- **Read** — Resolve `did:sns:alice.crbank.sol` → fetch from `attestto.id/{sns-name}/did.json` → verify SAS anchor hash
- **Update** — Update DID Document on CDN + re-anchor new hash on-chain
- **Deactivate** — Publish tombstone DID Document with `deactivated: true`, propagate via mesh in <500ms

## Compliance alignment

| Standard | Coverage |
|---|---|
| W3C DID Core 1.0 | Full |
| W3C VC Data Model v2.0 | Credential anchoring and presentation |
| SD-JWT (IETF draft) | Selective disclosure |
| FATF Travel Rule | Originator/beneficiary identification |
| eIDAS 2.0 | EU digital identity compliance target |
| ISO 20022 | Party identification in payment messages |
| GLEIF vLEI / ACDC / KERI | Institutional identity chain-of-trust |
| GDPR Article 17 | Right to erasure via crypto-shredding |
| Costa Rica Law 8968 | Data privacy |
| ML-DSA-44 / ML-KEM-768 | Post-quantum migration (planned) |

## Upstream contributions

This spec contributes to W3C and upstream DID methods to ensure cross-chain interoperability is standardized: 8 PRs to `did:ens`, 5 PRs to `did:pkh`, tracked at [W3C did-extensions #680](https://github.com/w3c/did-extensions/issues/680).
